title: The Critical Strip
mathematical_role: Give an exact symbolic analytic frame for the critical strip, critical line, pole, selected trivial zeros, and standard symmetries without inventing nontrivial-zero coordinates.
learning_objective: Locate the Riemann hypothesis in a memorable complex-plane landscape while separating exact symbolic structure from finite numerical zero data.
literal_semantics: The plate uses s = σ + it and labels Re(s) and Im(s).
The lines Re(s)=0, Re(s)=1/2, and Re(s)=1 are labelled.
The pole at s=1 is identified.
Selected trivial zeros -2 and -4 are exact.
The symmetries s ↔ 1−s and s ↔ s̄ are annotated.
No numerical nontrivial-zero coordinates are plotted.
nonliteral_semantics: The finite trivial-zero sample is not exhaustive.
The atmospheric glow and question marks are literary annotations, not data.
The plate does not encode zero multiplicities.

accessibility.alt_text: An illuminated complex-plane window shows the critical strip, gold critical line, pole at one, selected trivial zeros, and symmetry annotations; no nontrivial-zero dataset is plotted.
accessibility.long_description: A dark analytic window sits inside a parchment plate. The strip from real part zero to one is shaded, the half-line is gold, the pole and selected trivial zeros are marked, and faint question marks are explicitly non-data literary symbols.

supersession_reason: Replaces decorative zero dots with exact symbolic geography while retaining visual mystery without turning it into data.
